info.title: Soft Serve
info.description: The repositories on a Soft Serve server: reading them, and managing them with the same operations and permissions as the SSH `repo` commands. Every endpoint answers with what the caller may do: behind Outpost's login gateway the caller is the Soft Serve user named like the signed-in Outpost user; otherwise send a Soft Serve access token as `Authorization: Token <token>`, or nothing for anonymous access. A repository the caller may not read answers 404, like one that does not exist; to an anonymous caller, the management endpoints answer 401 instead, either way. Requests that change something are refused (403) when a browser says they come from another site. Bodies are JSON. Repository names can contain slashes, so the name and the action are separated by `/-/`.

get.summary: List the repositories the caller can read
get.description: Hidden repositories are left out unless asked for; they can still be fetched by name.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only repositories whose name, project name or description contains this, ignoring case

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: `true` to include hidden repositories, as `repo list --all` does

post.summary: Create a repository, or import one
post.description: With `remote`, the repository is imported from it: a hard fork that keeps no tie to the remote, or with `mirror` a mirror that keeps following it. Needs write access to the name.

patch.description: Only the fields sent change, in the order listed, stopping at the first that fails. Needs write access.

get.summary: A repository's settings and refs, as `repo info` shows them

post.description: Needs write access to the repository and to the new name.

post.summary: Pull a mirror from its upstream now
post.description: Needs write access. 400 if the repository is not a mirror, 409 if it is already syncing, 502 if the upstream could not be reached.

parameters.name: branch
parameters.description: Branch name; may contain slashes

delete.description: Not the default branch. Needs write access.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Tag name; may contain slashes

200.description: Branches (the default first, then most recently updated) and tags (newest first)

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Only commits that touched this file or directory

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only commits whose message contains this, 2 to 200 characters, matched as written and ignoring case

parameters.name: author
parameters.description: Only commits whose author's name or email contains this, ignoring case

get.summary: List or search commits reachable from a ref, newest first

parameters.name: sha
parameters.description: A full or abbreviated commit hash

parameters.name: ignore_whitespace
parameters.description: Leave out changes in whitespace

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Only this file's diff (by its new or old path), parsed in full rather than cut at 1,000 lines

get.summary: Get a commit, the files it changed and its patch

parameters.name: last_commits
parameters.description: Set to true for the latest commit of the directory and of each entry. It walks the history, so it is bounded: an entry not reached in time has none.

get.description: Up to 1 MiB of text inline; `truncated` says when there is more. A binary file has `binary` set and no content; fetch it from `/-/raw`.
Text is served as text/plain and binaries as attachments, so nothing in a repository renders as a page. A file tracked by Git LFS is served from the LFS store.

get.summary: Who last changed each line of a text file
get.description: Lines come in hunks, runs last changed by one commit; `commits` describes each. Binary files and files over 1 MiB are refused.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: Branch, tag or commit to compare against; the default branch when omitted

parameters.name: head
parameters.description: Branch, tag or commit whose changes to show

parameters.name: ignore_whitespace
parameters.description: Leave out changes in whitespace

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Only this file's diff (by its new or old path), parsed in full rather than cut at 1,000 lines

get.summary: What head has that base doesn't
get.description: The commits since head and base diverged (up to 250), and the diff from their merge base to head: what merging head into base would bring in.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Text to find, 2 to 200 characters, matched as written and ignoring case

get.summary: Find text in the files at a ref
get.description: Text files only. Up to 5 matching lines per file and 200 in all; `truncated` says when there were more.

get.summary: Download a snapshot of the files at a ref
get.description: Every file is under one directory named for the repository and ref. Files tracked by Git LFS are included as their pointers.

post.description: `access` defaults to read-write. Needs write access, and nobody but a server admin can grant more access than they have. To change someone's access, remove and add them again.

delete.description: Needs write access, and nobody but a server admin can remove someone with more access than they have.

get.description: Needs admin access. Secrets are never returned.

post.description: Needs admin access. The URL may not point at a private or local address.

patch.description: Only the fields sent change. Needs admin access.

get.summary: One delivery, with its request and response

get.description: Looked for in the root, then .github, then docs, preferring Markdown.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of a file's path, or its letters in order (`brgo` finds `browse.go`), 1 to 200 characters, ignoring case

get.summary: Find files at a ref by path
get.description: The closest matches first: in the file's name, then its path, then spread out. Up to 100.

parameters.name: owner_email
parameters.description: Author emails, comma-separated (up to 5), whose commits to count apart from everyone else's in `owner` and each week's `owner_commits`. Behind Outpost's login gateway, the signed-in user's email is used when this is left out. Either way, addresses the server's `author_aliases` config groups with these count too.

get.summary: Languages, size, contributors and weekly activity at a ref
get.description: Each count stops after 10 seconds on a very large repository; `partial` says when one did. With the caller's email known, the history is also split between their commits and everyone else's.
The caller's Soft Serve user, SSH keys, access tokens (never the tokens themselves) and the repositories they can push to. An anonymous caller gets `signed_in: false`.

patch.description: Your access, keys and tokens stay with the account.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key in authorized_keys form, or its SHA256 fingerprint

post.description: The answer is the only place the token appears; the server keeps only its hash.

delete.summary: Delete one of your access tokens

get.description: Server admins only; anyone else gets 401 or 403, whether or not the user exists.

post.description: Server admins only; anyone else gets 401 or 403, whether or not the user exists.

get.summary: A user and their SSH keys
get.description: Server admins only; anyone else gets 401 or 403, whether or not the user exists.

patch.summary: Change a user's admin flag or username
patch.description: The admin flag changes first, then the username. Admins can't remove their own admin flag. Server admins only; anyone else gets 401 or 403, whether or not the user exists.

delete.description: A user who owns repositories can't be deleted (409), and admins can't delete themselves (400). Server admins only; anyone else gets 401 or 403, whether or not the user exists.

post.summary: Add an SSH key to a user
post.description: Server admins only; anyone else gets 401 or 403, whether or not the user exists.

delete.summary: Remove an SSH key from a user
delete.description: Server admins only; anyone else gets 401 or 403, whether or not the user exists.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key in authorized_keys form, or its SHA256 fingerprint

patch.description: Server admins only. A setting the config file fixes is still saved, but the config wins; `*_fixed` says so.

200.description: All the settings, after the change

Ref.name: ref
Ref.description: Branch, tag or commit hash; the default branch when omitted

Path.name: path
Path.description: Path inside the repository; the root when omitted

empty.description: True when the repository has no commits yet

clone.description: How to clone. `https` is left out behind Outpost's login gateway, where git over HTTPS can't sign in; use SSH there.

mirror_of.description: Where a mirror is copied from, without credentials. Left out for a path on the server.

mirror_auto_sync.description: Whether a mirror syncs on the server's schedule, or only when someone runs `repo sync`. Left out for repositories that are not mirrors.

commit.description: The commit it points at (peeled, for an annotated tag)

date.description: When a branch's tip was committed, or a tag made

message.description: An annotated tag's message, without its signature

ahead.description: Commits this branch has that the default branch doesn't. Left out for the default branch, for tags, and when there wasn't time to count.

behind.description: Commits the default branch has that this branch doesn't

path.description: The path the history is limited to, if any

total.description: Commits reachable from ref that pass the filters given

path.description: The file the diff was limited to, if any

lfs.description: Tracked by Git LFS; size and content are the stored file's

lfs_missing.description: Tracked by Git LFS, but the object was never pushed here; content is the pointer

truncated.description: The file's diff was cut short, past 1,000 lines; ask for it alone with `path` to see all of it

commits.description: The commits the hunks name, by hash

start.description: Line number of the first line, from 1

merge_base.description: Where head and base diverged; equal to head_commit when head has nothing new

patch.description: Unified diff from merge_base to head, up to 1 MiB

path.description: The file the diff was limited to, if any

more.description: Matches in this file past the ones shown

RepoSettings.description: A repository's settings and refs, as `repo info` shows them

auto_sync.description: For a mirror: whether it syncs on the server's schedule, or only when asked

default_branch.description: Left out for a repository with no commits

mirror.description: With remote: keep following it, rather than a hard fork

auto_sync.description: With mirror: sync on the server's schedule. Defaults to true

lfs.description: With remote: pull Git LFS objects

lfs_endpoint.description: With remote: the Git LFS endpoint

WebhookOptions.description: When creating: url and events are needed, content_type defaults to json and active to true. When changing: only the fields sent change.

CommitSignature.description: How a commit was signed. An SSH signature is verified when it is good and made with a key some user on this server has; that says nothing of the commit's author or committer fields. GPG and X.509 signatures aren't checked.

signer.description: The Soft Serve user whose key made a verified signature

key.description: SHA256 fingerprint of an SSH signature's key

languages.description: Largest first, by bytes. Vendored code, prose and data formats are left out.

contributors.description: The 25 most frequent authors, by commits, leaving out merges

weekly.description: Commits in each of the last 52 weeks, oldest first; weeks start on Monday, UTC

owner_commits.description: How many of them are the caller's; left out when none are, or the caller's email isn't known

owner.description: The history split between the caller's commits, by author email, and everyone else's. Left out when the caller's email isn't known.

first.description: When the caller's first commit here was made

outpost_user.description: Who Outpost's login gateway says the caller is, when it fronts this server

repos.description: Repositories the user can push to or administer

expires_at.description: Unset for a token that never expires
